title: Executive Summary
description: Bottom line for Rental increase SF, starting with the Rent Board license question, with every finding linked to an official source.

sections.title: Question first: Rent Board license for an individual owner

rows.label: Do I need a Rent Board license as an individual owner (no corporation)?
rows.value: Yes. A current Rent Increase License must be on file before an annual or banked increase takes effect; no individual-owner, small-portfolio or fewer-than-10-unit exemption was found.
rows.notes: Requirement follows the rent-controlled status of the unit, not the size of the owner.

rows.label: Must I report to the Rent Board before notifying tenants?
rows.value: Yes. Report each unit into the Housing Inventory (buildings under 10 units since March 1, 2023; every March 1 after that); the license is generated from that report.
rows.notes: No separate filing of the increase notice itself is described.

rows.label: What happens if I notice an increase without a current license?
rows.value: The notice may be null and void, the tenant may be owed a refund, and the tenant may petition the Rent Board for an Administrative Law Judge hearing.
rows.notes: Tenants can check license status in the Rent Board Portal.

rows.label: Step-by-step process
rows.value: 12 numbered steps from coverage check to notice delivery, each with its official link
rows.notes: Published on the Step-by-Step License page.

rows.label: Banked increases
rows.value: Only if >=24 full months without any increase; add percentages, do not compound/prorate
rows.notes: No banked amount inferred for this case.
